neighbours.label: ' just' meaning 'merely for' a trivial purpose or reason ('just to', 'just for', 'just because') after a costly act
fire: He quit a stable job just to chase a rumor about gold.
Nobody should risk their health just for a few extra dollars.
They tore down the old library just to build a parking lot.
She refused to lie just because her boss asked her to.
Why would you drive four hours just for a sandwich?
The senator blocked the bill just to embarrass the governor.
I won't give up my weekend just so you can sleep in.
Don't throw away a good friendship just over a silly argument.
quiet: He had just finished a stable job when the call came.
Nobody was hurt; the car just missed the fence.
The old library is just across the street from the park.
She was just about to leave when her boss called.
The sandwich tasted just like the one my grandmother made.
The senator arrived just in time for the vote.
My weekend was just perfect, thanks for asking.
That friendship is just as strong as it was in school.

notes: Probes: 'sacrifice her career just to' 0.83, 'just because' 0.33; temporal/degree 'just' ~0.
